text: FORMAL SYNC: repository-owner reclassification of the migration-bridge pipeline, effective 2026-09-01. The database/container interchange and migration-bridge pipeline (umbrella #137, covering #138 Access/VBA migration bridge, #139 .NET execution/interop bridge, #140 IMPORT/EXPORT DATABASE TYPE JSON/SQL, #141 IMPORT/EXPORT DATABASE TYPE ACCESS, #1076 interpret legacy xBase/Fox Software assets, #1077 produce binaries for legacy xBase/Fox Software products) is now an ACTIVE VERSION 1 BLOCKING CRITERION, not work sequenced after v1 as previously documented. This came from a direct repository-owner instruction relayed through an architecture-review report (from reviewer 'agy'). Before acting on it, I verified the live issue bodies against the request and found they explicitly said the opposite ('sequenced after Version 1... not part of it') -- flagged this conflict to the user rather than writing contradictory docs, and the user confirmed: reconcile the issues first. All 7 issue bodies (#137, #138, #139, #140, #141, #1076, #1077) updated on GitHub to reflect the new blocking status, keeping the existing 'real, committed, not optional' framing from the earlier #5413 wishlist-framing correction intact -- only the sequencing changed. Docs updated to match: docs/01-product-charter.md (Version target note, and the Non-Goals section which previously listed producing legacy-format binaries as an explicit non-goal -- directly contradicted #1077's new status, now corrected), docs/03-compatibility-and-migration.md (Version target note), agents.md (Product And Roadmap Intent section). PR #5437 open against v1-development, not yet merged. BOTH AGENTS: re-sequence your intake queues to treat this pipeline as part of the active v1 critical path -- when selecting the highest-value unfinished subgoal per docs/05's roadmap sequencing rule, #137's children are now eligible alongside VFP 9 parity-closure work, not deferred behind it. Do not pick up #137/#138/#139/#140/#141/#1076/#1077 work until PR #5437 merges (keeps agent-handoff.md/docs consistent with the issues), but do factor the new priority into any current sequencing decisions now.
